equity_bridge.item: Investment securities (cross-shareholdings and equity-method stakes), after tax on embedded gains
equity_bridge.note: JPY54,682m at 2026-06-30 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin balance sheet), carried at fair value for AFS holdings; AOCI valuation difference JPY29.0bn net of tax implies ~JPY12-13bn of deferred tax on embedded gains, so JPY45bn is taken as the realisable after-tax value. The company is actively selling (proceeds JPY20.4bn FY2026, JPY18.4bn FY2025). Matching rule: dividend income and equity-method profit sit below operating profit and are outside the EBITDA-based flows.
2026-06-30 balance sheet. Charged once, here; flows are consolidated.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Near-term base-case revenue growth, anchored to FY2027 guidance (+2.7%) and the 3-yr revenue CAGR (2.5%); the 5-yr figure (8.0%) is inflated by yen depreciation from ~106 to ~151 per USD over FY2021-FY2026 and by the FY2021 COVID trough base.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (6.4% 3-yr, 8.4% 5-yr) diverges >30% from revenue (2.5% 3-yr) and EPS. Both are distorted: equity is lifted by foreign-currency translation gains (FCTA +JPY69bn in AOCI) and the 5-yr base sits just after the FY2021 Polyplastics minority buyout cut net assets by ~JPY160bn; EPS CAGRs are dominated by the FY2026 JPY32.4bn impairment (normalised FY2026 EPS ex-impairment is ~JPY125, giving roughly -3% 3-yr and +14% 5-yr). Neither equity nor EPS CAGR is used as the growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series equals reported FCF (OCF less PP&E and intangible purchases): SBC is immaterial and already inside operating profit, and interest income is not stripped for a net-debt company. FCF CAGRs are not computable (FY2023 base -25.1bn; FY2021 base 21.1bn to FY2026 -0.2bn) -- reported FCF has been near zero or negative in four of the last five years during the Polyplastics/COC capex programme (capex JPY47-72bn/yr against D&A JPY27-43bn). FCF in millions JPY: FY2021 21,080; FY2022 -4,478; FY2023 -25,076; FY2024 7,521; FY2025 21,064; FY2026 -178.

scenario_narratives.base: Daicel is a diversified chemicals group whose value now rests on three things: engineering plastics (HPP, 44% of sales) growing with AI-server, EV and medical content; Safety (airbag inflators) lifting its margin from ~6% toward management's 15% target on China/India volume and productivity; and the Materials segment (acetate tow, acetyl chain) managing a structural decline against Chinese capacity. Base assumes revenue grows 2.5-3.5% in a stable-yen world, the EBITDA margin recovers from the FY2026-27 trough (14.6%) to 16.5% -- the 10-year average less a haircut, crediting about half of the Accelerate 2030 self-help -- and capex falls from JPY63.5bn (FY2027 guidance) to ~8% of revenue (~1.05x D&A) by FY2031, slightly above the plan's ~JPY47bn/yr run-rate. Owner FCF therefore climbs from ~JPY6bn in FY2027 to ~JPY30bn+ by FY2031; the first five years of this decade produce little cash and most of the value is in the terminal, which is capped at 15x FCF (Gordon at 7%/1.5% would allow ~18.5x). Working capital at 39% of revenue is assumed to keep absorbing cash as the business grows.
scenario_narratives.bull: Accelerate 2030 is delivered: HPP EBITDA hits JPY45bn by FY2028 and keeps compounding on AI-server LCP/PPS and EV PBT/PPS wins; Safety reaches a 15% operating margin and 30% inflator share by FY2030; COC turns to breakeven as EU PPWR packaging demand arrives; capex settles at the plan's ~JPY47bn/yr with no overruns; the inventory-reduction programme limits working-capital drag. EBITDA margin returns to the 18% of FY2017-2018 and revenue compounds 5-6% for several years. Terminal cap 16x with 2.0% growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: Yen strength, an auto downturn and Chinese overcapacity arrive together: revenue stalls for two years and the EBITDA margin sits at the 13.5-14% FY2020-21 trough; capex stays near JPY60bn as COC and CO-plant remediation continue; working capital keeps consuming cash. FCF hovers at JPY0-15bn for most of the decade and the terminal is capped at 12x. Because net debt is JPY238bn (2.8x FY2026 EBITDA), the equity residual approaches zero in this path even though the company is not insolvent (interest cover ~13x on JPY2.9bn of interest paid).

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Daicel on what an owner can take out after the capex programme, not on the P/E the market quotes. FY2026 earnings are impairment-depressed, but the DCF starts above that line (EBITDA) so the impairment matters only as evidence on execution. The honest picture is a leveraged, moderately cyclical chemicals group whose free cash flow has been consumed by five years of Polyplastics/COC investment and a 39%-of-sales working-capital base; the equity is worth what it is because capex is guided to fall by a third and margins to recover. The terminal is capped at 12-16x FCF so the valuation does not depend on a re-rating, and risk is charged once -- in the scenario flows and weights, not by stacking a premium on the JPY-built WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capex path: every 1pp of revenue that capex stays above the modelled 8% long-run level removes roughly JPY6-7bn/yr of owner FCF, around a fifth of the base terminal cash flow; Accelerate 2030 is a JPY250bn envelope that management is already 'reviewing'.
Leverage amplifies everything: with JPY238bn of net debt, a 1pp swing in long-run EBITDA margin moves equity value by roughly 15-20% in the base case, and the bear case leaves little equity residual.

Margin recovery to 16.5% relies on Safety's margin tripling and COC's loss closing; both are management targets, not contracted outcomes, and the growth-driver EBITDA target was cut from +50% to +30% within days of being announced.
Yen: guidance assumes JPY150/USD; a return toward JPY130 would compress JPY-reported sales and margins (overseas plants in Germany, the US, China and India).
Structural decline of acetate tow (tobacco) and Chinese overcapacity in acetyl/POM may run faster than the modest revenue path assumes.
Working capital: inventories are 32% of revenue; the model assumes no release, but a further build (as in Q1 FY2027, +JPY12.5bn) would push FCF back toward zero.
Equity bridge items (investment securities JPY45bn after tax, NCI JPY15.5bn) together are ~JPY115/share and are taken at balance-sheet values.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1112.5-1658.0 JPY
data_sources.financials: 4202.T_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, millions JPY) for FY2015-FY2026 and Q1 FY2027; FY2026 tanshin (4202.T_Annual_FY2026.txt) for the cash-flow components, share counts and restricted-stock expense; Q1 FY2027 tanshin (4202.T_Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt) for the 2026-06-30 balance sheet and share count; Q1 FY2027 presentation for FY2027 guidance by segment and the capex/D&A forecast (JPY63.5bn / JPY44.0bn); Materials segment briefing 2026-08-21 for the Accelerate 2030 capital-investment envelope (JPY80bn + 115bn + 55bn).
data_sources.qualitative: 4202.T_Analysis.json (2026-10-31): segment mix, Accelerate 2030 targets, bull/bear axes, risk register.

inputs.share_count_basis: 256,142,682 issued less 749,322 treasury at 2026-06-30 (Q1 FY2027 tanshin, after the FY2027 cancellation of 10.8m treasury shares). FY2026 tanshin states diluted EPS is not presented because there are no dilutive shares, so basic = fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is immaterial and already expensed; buybacks (JPY13.8bn FY2026, JPY15.0bn FY2025) are treated as value-neutral.
inputs.net_debt_note: 2026-06-30 balance sheet: short-term borrowings 41,569 + short-term bonds 14,000 + current LT borrowings 14,255 + bonds 70,000 + LT borrowings 170,949 = 310,773; cash and deposits 73,032. Lease obligations (~JPY8bn, inside 'Other' liabilities) deliberately EXCLUDED because lease payments are charged in the flows (treatment B).
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 tanshin, statement of changes in equity: restricted stock awards JPY479m (0.08% of revenue). J-GAAP books this expense inside SG&A, so the operating profit from which EBITDA is derived already bears it; it is not deducted a second time (sbc_incl_equity_taxes = 0) and the forward sbc_pct_path is held at an explicit 0.0%. Effectively an SBC-zero filer: house and street bases coincide.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income JPY816m is NOT stripped: the company is net debt (JPY237.7bn), so there is no cash pile being double-counted. Dividend income (JPY2.4bn) and equity-method profit (JPY2.5bn) sit below operating profit in J-GAAP and are therefore already outside the EBITDA-based flows; their source asset (investment securities) is added in equity_bridge instead.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in JPY, the currency of the flows. 10y JGB ~1.8%, Japan ERP ~6.0%, levered beta ~1.2 for a leveraged cyclical chemicals/auto-components group -> cost of equity ~9.0%. Cost of debt: FY2026 interest paid JPY2.9bn on ~JPY300bn average debt = ~1.0% pre-tax, ~0.7% after tax. Market weights (equity JPY371bn / debt JPY311bn) give a mechanical WACC of ~5.2%; a 70/30 target structure gives ~6.5%. House reference for JPY keiretsu industrials is ~9%, but that is effectively an all-equity rate for net-cash suppliers. 7.0% is used: the 70/30 figure rounded up to reflect ND/EBITDA of 2.8x and the capex-execution record (FY2026 COC impairment). Risk is charged here ONCE -- the same WACC is used in all three scenarios; cyclicality and execution risk are carried in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked as a further premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. J-GAAP filer: operating leases are already expensed inside operating profit. Finance-lease principal repayments (JPY1,642m FY2026, 0.28% of revenue) are charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease obligations are excluded from net debt. ROU depreciation is immaterial at this scale so D&A is not adjusted for it.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI deducted ONCE in the equity bridge at book value (JPY15,478m at 2026-06-30). Flows are consolidated (EBITDA basis) so no attributable-only leakage is applied. Continuity note: Polyplastics' 45% minority (Celanese) was bought out in FY2021 for ~JPY160bn, which is why net assets dropped from JPY381bn (H1 FY2021) to JPY222bn (9M FY2021) and debt jumped from JPY105bn to JPY276bn. Pre-FY2021 attributable net income/EPS exclude ~45% of Polyplastics' profit (NCI dividends ran JPY4-8bn/yr) and are not comparable with later years; consolidated revenue, EBITDA and FCF are comparable across the break. The April 2026 absorption of Polyplastics into Daicel was a merger of a wholly owned subsidiary and has no NCI effect. Residual NCI (~JPY2.5bn profit share FY2026) relates to other subsidiaries.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon (FY2027-FY2036), per dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the adaptations file applied (JPY WACC, lease treatment B, NCI in bridge, investment securities in bridge, SBC-zero). FY2026 reported net income (JPY10.2bn) is depressed by a JPY32.4bn non-cash COC plant impairment booked below operating profit; the model starts from EBITDA (JPY85.4bn, 14.7% margin), which the impairment does not touch, so no normalisation of net income is needed in the flows -- the impairment's only valuation footprint is as evidence on capex execution, reflected in the WACC round-up and the 25% bear weight. FY2027 guidance (sales JPY595.0bn, OP JPY42.5bn, EBITDA JPY87.0bn, D&A JPY44.0bn, capex JPY63.5bn, NI JPY32.0bn) anchors year 1. Accelerate 2030 (~JPY250bn capital investment FY2027-2031, i.e. ~JPY47bn/yr after FY2027) is used only as a sense-check that capex can fall toward ~8% of revenue; the base path is more conservative than the plan. Working capital: receivables + inventories - payables = JPY230bn (39% of revenue, inventories alone 32%), so growth consumes cash (negative wc_capture); management's inventory-reduction programme is NOT credited as a release. Price is the 30 Oct 2026 regular close; Japan's market was shut on the valuation date (Saturday). FY2026 segment figures were restated into the new five-segment structure; totals are unchanged. Reported FCF has been negative or near zero in four of the last five fiscal years (FY2022 -4.5bn, FY2023 -25.1bn, FY2024 +7.5bn, FY2025 +21.1bn, FY2026 -0.2bn) during the Polyplastics/COC capex programme; the valuation therefore rests on capex normalising, and the sensitivity to that path is the single biggest judgment in the file.

bear.narrative: A stronger yen (guidance assumes JPY150/USD; the model's flows are JPY so translation shrinks reported sales), a global auto-production downturn hitting Safety and HPP volumes, continued Chinese price pressure in acetate tow, POM and acetic acid, and a repeat of CO-plant outages hold revenue flat for two years and the EBITDA margin at the FY2020-2021 trough (13.5-14%). Capex stays elevated for longer as COC and CO-plant fixes absorb cash, and working capital keeps consuming cash. With JPY238bn of net debt the equity residual is thin.

base.growth_rationale: Y1 = FY2027 guidance (JPY595.0bn, +2.7%). Y2-Y3 3.5% as High Performance Polymers (AI-server LCP/PPS, EV content) and Safety (China/India installation rates) outgrow a shrinking Materials segment (acetate tow); fades to 2% by Y8 as auto content growth matures. Assumes a broadly stable yen around the JPY150 planning rate.
base.margin_rationale: Y1 14.6% = FY2027 guided EBITDA JPY87.0bn / JPY595bn. Ramps to 16.5% by Y5, the 10-yr average (16.9%) less a haircut: management's own levers (HPP EBITDA JPY34.3bn -> 45.0bn by FY2028, Safety margin 6% -> 15% by FY2030, COC loss -12bn -> breakeven by FY2031) would sum to ~17.5-18% if all delivered; base credits roughly half of that uplift.
base.capex_rationale: Y1 10.7% = FY2027 forecast JPY63.5bn. Falls to 8.0% (~1.05x D&A) by Y5 and holds -- Accelerate 2030's ~JPY250bn over FY2027-2031 implies ~JPY47bn/yr (~7.5%) after FY2027, so the base path is above plan to allow for the overrun pattern (COC second plant).
base.wc_rationale: Net working capital 39% of revenue; incremental NWC assumed at 20% of each year's revenue increase (negative capture = cash consumed). No credit for the inventory-reduction programme.
base.tax_rationale: Japan statutory effective rate ~30.6%; FY2026 cash taxes (JPY25.0bn) were inflated by arrears on FY2025 profits and securities-sale gains, so 31% flat is used from Y1.

bull.narrative: Management delivers Accelerate 2030: HPP EBITDA reaches JPY45bn by FY2028 on AI-server and EV content, Safety hits a 15% operating margin and 30% share by FY2030, COC reaches breakeven, capex falls to the ~JPY47bn/yr plan run-rate with no further overruns, and inventory discipline holds incremental working capital to 15% of growth. EBITDA margin returns to the FY2017-2018 range (18%+).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: net debt of JPY238bn (2.8x EBITDA) against a business that has produced near-zero FCF for five years, a demonstrated capex-execution problem (JPY32.4bn COC impairment, CO-plant outages, missed 'super asset-light' targets), and cyclical exposure to autos, Chinese chemical pricing and the yen. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it requires several independent things to go right at once -- the HPP EBITDA target, the Safety margin tripling, the COC turnaround and capex discipline -- and management already trimmed the growth-driver EBITDA target within days of announcing it. Base 50%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
